counterfactual_missing_items: histological confirmation of the gallbladder primary is not supplied
definitive biopsy of a pulmonary nodule is not supplied
an explicit alternative diagnosis for the liver mass is not supplied
decisive_items: a distended gallbladder with poor delineation of the posterior wall, appearing large, solid, and heterogeneous with posterior dense shadowing and calcific components
a 10-cm calcified gallbladder wall invading liver segments 4 and 5
multiple pulmonary nodules consistent with metastatic disease (T4 N1 M1)
response.rationale: R2 is the most complete causal-anatomic diagnosis: the calcified invasive gallbladder wall plus solid heterogeneous gallbladder mass locate the primary tumour and explain the liver invasion and metastases. R3 describes only the downstream pulmonary-CT finding and does not identify the primary site, so it is a complication/staging label rather than the most likely diagnosis.

rejected.why: Metastatic disease is a stage/mechanism of the gallbladder cancer and is directly explained by the invasive gallbladder mass; it lacks the primary source and is therefore not the best diagnosis.
